name: First Player Tokens
what_it_is: A token shows who goes first in the turn order.
needs_to_really_work: The game must have a changing turn order across rounds and the token must be passed according to clear rules. For orders with more than two positions, more markers or an order track may be needed.
just_a_label_when: A token that stays with one player or is ignored because the order never changes.
knobs: how the token is passed; how many positions in the order need markers
can_cause: Bookkeeping Tokens

name: Goal Indicators
what_it_is: Information that shows the player what their current goals are.
needs_to_really_work: They must give accurate, timely information about goals and progress toward them, in a form players can read at a glance. The information must connect to something players can act on.
just_a_label_when: A quest log or marker that is vague, outdated or hidden, so players still don't know what to do or how close they are.
knobs: how much detail is shown; how precise (exact vs vague); how often it is updated
can_cause: Game State Overviews
caused_by: Check Points; Closure Points; Cutscenes; Narration Structures; Progress Indicators

name: Tooltips
what_it_is: An explanation shown when the player pays attention to a game element.
needs_to_really_work: The text must contain information that actually helps decisions, appear at the right moment and with the right delay, and not flood the player. It should cover the elements players are likely to be unsure about.
just_a_label_when: A popup that merely repeats the item's name or flavour text and teaches nothing about how it works.
knobs: which elements get tips; how much detail; hover delay before showing
can_cause: Clues; Non-Diegetic Features; Strategic Planning
caused_by: Mediated Gameplay

name: Outcome Indicators
what_it_is: Extra signals about how an action ended, beyond its effect in the world.
needs_to_really_work: There must be an outcome that players cannot easily read from the world itself, and the indicator must report it clearly and at the right time. The detail level can be varied to keep some uncertainty.
just_a_label_when: An indicator that repeats what is already obvious on screen, or one that appears too late or too vaguely to help players understand what happened.
knobs: what outcomes are indicated; how precise the information is; how long and when it is shown
can_cause: Game State Indicators; Predictable Consequences
caused_by: Near Miss Indicators

name: Explicit Random Seeds
what_it_is: The player can enter the number from which the game builds its randomness.
needs_to_really_work: The game must have a seeded random generator and show a clear way for players to enter and share the seed. The same seed then has to give the same results every time.
just_a_label_when: A seed field exists, but the game mixes in the clock or other randomness, so identical seeds give different worlds.
knobs: what the seed controls (whole world, level layout, just a setup); how visible the seed input is
can_cause: Freedom of Choice
caused_by: Game Worlds

name: Loading Hints
what_it_is: Game tips that are shown while the game is loading.
needs_to_really_work: There must be waiting moments, and the hints must be useful, correct and varied enough to be read. They should connect to what the player will do next.
just_a_label_when: Vague or repeated tips, or generic lore lines, that teach nothing about play.
knobs: how many hints; how they are chosen; how long they display
can_cause: Clues; Strategic Planning
changes: Complex Gameplay; Downtime; Predetermined Story Structures; Strategic Knowledge

name: Rabbit Hole Invitations
what_it_is: A vague invitation that draws a person into a particular game.
needs_to_really_work: The cryptic messages must be placed where target players will find them and be intriguing enough to follow. Several are spread over media and time since individual ones may be missed.
just_a_label_when: A clue is posted, but it is too obscure or in the wrong place, so nobody finds or follows it.
knobs: how many; where posted; how cryptic; timing

name: Current Player Tokens
what_it_is: A token showing whose turn it is.
needs_to_really_work: The token must be clearly visible and the rules must say exactly when it passes. It is most useful when turns are long or players act out of turn.
just_a_label_when: A token that sits on the table but is passed late or ignored, while players still ask whose turn it is.
knobs: token size and visibility; the exact moment it is handed over
can_cause: Bookkeeping Tokens

name: Meta-Postures
what_it_is: Agreed poses and gestures convey information about the game without breaking character.
needs_to_really_work: The gestures must be few, easy to learn, clearly different from each other and visible without breaking the fiction. Everyone must know the meanings.
just_a_label_when: A list of gestures on paper that players forget or ignore, so they keep speaking out of character anyway.
knobs: how many gestures; how distinct and how visible they are

name: Self-Reported Positioning
what_it_is: The player's physical location matters in the game, but the player reports it to the game themselves.
needs_to_really_work: Players need a way to report their location, and the game should use that location for something. Trust or checks decide whether reports can be false.
just_a_label_when: A check-in button whose reported place has no effect on anything in the game.
knobs: how location is reported; how often; whether reports are checked
can_cause: Self-Facilitated Games; Social Adaptability; Casual Gameplay

name: Prompting Techniques
what_it_is: In role-playing: lines that hint how to change the scene without leaving character.
needs_to_really_work: The group needs shared, easily noticed signals that fit the fiction, learned before play. Different scenes may need different prompts.
just_a_label_when: Signals are listed in the rulebook, but nobody notices or uses them, so players still break character to change scenes.
knobs: which signals exist; how subtle they are; who may use them
